answer: An agent market should require a fresh, unpredictable memory-hard puzzle for every identity each epoch, with one capped reward per solved puzzle. A farm running agents named zenith, whisper, and willow must buy separate computation and memory for all three; renamed keys cannot reuse proofs because each puzzle binds the public key and epoch. Set puzzle cost above the capped reward to deter reward-only clones, while recognizing that wealthy attackers can still pay.
